"As Shot" (the camera's setting), "Auto" (computed from the image), or for raw/DNG "Daylight", "Cloudy", "Shade", "Tungsten", "Fluorescent", "Flash"; "Custom" when Temp/Tint were set by hand. Temperature and Tint only take effect when this is not "As Shot" (Ambrotype's edit commands switch it to "Custom" when you set Temp or Tint).

"color" for colour negative film (orange base), "bw" for black-and-white negatives, "positive" for slide (reversal) film: no inversion, and the levels take out the light's colour. A black-and-white film stock also gives a black-and-white result.

-9 to 9: a camera-style white balance shift along blue, on top of whatever white balance is set (As Shot too), so it works in a preset. Blue minus red cools by 4 mireds a step; red plus blue adds magenta, 3 Tint a step (ours, not measured).

-9 to 9: a camera-style white balance shift along red, on top of whatever white balance is set (As Shot too), so it works in a preset. Red minus blue warms by 4 mireds a step; red plus blue adds magenta, 3 Tint a step (ours, not measured).

0 to 100: how far the measured levels move so the frame's greys come out grey. Red and blue are matched to green on the least saturated colour at five levels from shadows to highlights, instead of assuming the darkest shadow and brightest highlight are grey (ours). Stored levels already include it (Freeze, Sync negative roll); does nothing on black-and-white film.
